name: Levodropropizine + Chlorpheniramine
meta: Per 5 mL: Levodropropizine 30 mg + Chlorpheniramine maleate 2 mg
Prescription-only fixed-dose combination. Components – Levodropropizine: Schedule
H – prescription only; Chlorpheniramine Maleate: Schedule H – prescription only
sections: White crystalline powder (maleate), freely soluble in water.

Levodropropizine: The levo-isomer of dropropizine; meta-analyses suggest greater efficacy than central antitussives (codeine, dextromethorphan) with less somnolence. First approval/introduction: Introduced in Italy 1988 (Dompé).

Chlorpheniramine Maleate: One of the most widely used first-generation antihistamines; on the WHO List of Essential Medicines. First approval/introduction: Patented 1948; medical use from 1949 (Schering).
Per 5 mL: Levodropropizine 30 mg + Chlorpheniramine maleate 2 mg
Peripheral antitussive with low central sedation, combined with an antihistamine to control allergic triggers of cough.

Levodropropizine Acts peripherally on tracheobronchial sensory C-fibres, inhibiting release of sensory neuropeptides and reducing the cough reflex without central sedation or respiratory depression. Receptor / target profile: Peripheral antitussive acting on capsaicin-sensitive C-fibre afferents of the cough reflex; inhibits release of sensory neuropeptides.

Chlorpheniramine Maleate Competitive H1 antagonist with anticholinergic action, reducing rhinorrhoea, sneezing, itching and lacrimation. Receptor / target profile: Potent H1 inverse agonist with weak antimuscarinic activity and some serotonin reuptake inhibition.
Summary: Bioavailability >75%; Tmax 0.25–0.75 h. Low protein binding (11–14%). Half-life 1–2 h.
Summary: Well absorbed; Tmax 2.5–6 h. Hepatic metabolism. Half-life 12–43 h.
Dry, non-productive cough with allergic component (rhinitis, post-nasal drip)
Cough due to upper respiratory tract infection or bronchitis (non-productive)
Adults: 10 mL three times daily at intervals of at least 6 h
Children: per body weight as directed (not under 2 years)
Dose to be individualised by the treating physician according to clinical response and tolerability.
Use with caution in severe impairment.
Not for <2 years; 2–6 years per specialist.
Bronchorrhoea, impaired mucociliary function (Kartagener's syndrome, ciliary dyskinesia)
Concomitant or recent (14 days) MAO inhibitors
Chlorpheniramine Maleate: With food; avoid alcohol.
Levodropropizine: Supportive care. Chlorpheniramine Maleate: CNS depression or excitation (children), anticholinergic effects, convulsions. Supportive care.
Zanasi et al., Multidiscip Respir Med 2015 – meta-analysis: levodropropizine more effective than central antitussives with less somnolence.
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
